subject: Usage snapshot discrepancy / VAT reconciliation for Aug invoice
messages:
From: Marco Santini <marco.santini@lumina.tech>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumina Tech Billing <billing@lumina.tech>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Unexplained usage + VAT change on Aug invoice

Hi Evelyn,

We've just reviewed our August invoice (INV-2027-08-4453) and there are two items that don't line up with our internal logs: first, an unexpected jump in embed/token usage starting Aug 18 that we don't see on our side; second, VAT on the disputed lines is being calculated under a different entity assumption than we expected (we're EU B2B reverse-charge eligible).

Attached is a CSV extract from our ingestion logs for Aug 15–31 (short sample) and the invoice line items we think are affected. Can you confirm:
- How the mediated token counts are attributed for post-pay customers when replay/ingest reprocessing occurs mid-period?
- Whether any model routing or auxiliary reranking (fallbacks) could have generated additional tokens billed to our org on Aug 18–20?

This is blocking our AP team from processing the payment. We need an evidence export showing the server-side request ids for the charged tokens and a VAT position confirmation before we can clear the invoice.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

—Marco
Marco Santini
Head of Platform Ops
Lumina Tech
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Santini <marco.santini@lumina.tech>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 10:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexplained usage + VAT change on Aug invoice

Hi Marco — thanks for the note and the sample. Sorry for the trouble — we'll treat this as high priority. Quick answers up front:

- Post-pay ingest replays can create billable tokens if replayed into production model endpoints; we have safeguards but they rely on request id tagging and tenant attribution.
- Model routing fallbacks (e.g., to a larger variant) can incur additional tokens; those are normally surfaced in the detailed usage export per request id.

Jonas (finance) and Kimberly (AE) are looped in. To expedite: could you send a CSV with the Lumina request ids for Aug 18–20 (a small sample of ~20 rows is fine) and confirm whether those requests came from your staging or production keys? If you prefer, we can run a server-side request_id match and provide a signed export.

We'll also run an initial delta analysis and share the earliest findings by EOD Monday. If VAT needs adjustment for reverse-charge we will coordinate with our tax team and propose a credit (or invoice reversal) as appropriate.

Attachments: none

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0190

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Santini <marco.santini@lumina.tech>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 16:20:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexplained usage + VAT change on Aug invoice

Hi Marco — quick update from finance/ops after matching Lumina's sample against our request-store. Summary:

1) We matched 39 of 40 provided request_ids to server-side entries. One id (lum-req-8951) had a near-duplicate (lum-req-8951-1) in our logs caused by a client retry where the original request was resent with the same payload but without idempotency header; both attempts were billed. We've flagged this as a product-behavior note (idempotency enforcement gap).

2) On Aug 18–19 we see an automated fallback routing event for a short window (13:58–15:10 UTC) where certain requests were routed to a larger model variant due to a transient cache miss on the small model pool. That produced additional tokens for some calls; we show a delta of 1,248 billed tokens across the matched sample window.

3) VAT position: Lumina's account is configured as EU B2B; however, the invoice engine applied reverse-charge only to line-level items tagged under entity_id: redwood-eu-legacy. For the lines impacted by the fallback/dedup, the system attributed billing to the global hosted entity (redwood-hosted-us) which triggered standard VAT calculation. That is incorrect for Lumina and we accept responsibility.

Proposed remediation:
- We will issue a credit equal to the VAT applied on the misattributed lines (~€3,150) and apply a pro-rated credit for the duplicate attempt billing where applicable (~€26). Total proposed credit: €3,176.
- We will reissue a corrected invoice with reverse-charge applied to the affected lines and mark the original as superseded.
- Product will deploy an idempotency header enforcement check and a routing guard to prevent model-fallback billing for requests that should remain on the small model when cache misses are detected (ETA: 2 weeks).

Attached is a short analysis PDF (usage_delta_analysis.pdf) with matching tables and the server-side evidence export (request ids, timestamps, model_variant).

Next steps: please confirm you accept the proposed credit and reissue approach and whether you want the credit applied to the outstanding invoice or kept as a balance for Oct. Once we have your confirmation we will: (a) post the credit, (b) reissue invoice INV-2027-08-4453-rev1, and (c) unblock payment collection.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll also run a small reconciliation call if useful.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_delta_analysis.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
